subject: Power analysis Mimic model.... error messages

messages.author: 6283bd86a46e829b
messages.subject: Power analysis Mimic model.... error messages
parts:
Dear all:

I try to run a power analysis for a MIMIC model. 

I keep getting the following error messages : 

 In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  ... :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

Did I do something wrong in the syntax?

My Syntax:

population.model1 <- 'f =~ 0.553*x1 + 0.705*x2 + 0.621*x3 + 0.884*x4 + -0.805*x5 
f ~ 0.095*y
f ~ 0.265*z'
model <- 'f =~ NA*x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 
f ~ y
f ~ z'
nsims <- 500
significant<-rep(NA,nsims)
set.seed(237829)
for (i in 1:nsims){
  myData <- simulateData(population.model1,sample.nobs=104,standardized=T)
  fit <- cfa(model,data=myData)
  z <- inspect(fit,"est")$lambda[1,1]/inspect(fit,"se")$lambda[1,1]
  ifelse(inspect(fit,"converged")==TRUE,significant[i]<-((1-pnorm(abs(z)))*2)<.05,NA)
}
table(significant)

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Power analysis Mimic model.... error messages
parts:
You haven't set the scale of f in the analysis model. There are two built in options in lavaan: a marker variable method (setting a factor loading to 1) or a fixed factor method (setting the latent variance/residual variance to 1). By default the cfa command will use a marker variable method, but in your code you overwrote that (by using the NA label on the first factor loading). Either add std.lv=TRUE to the cfa function in your loop, or remove the NA* from the model syntax and things should run fine.*

Alex

* Fun fact, tests of significance (using a Wald test) will differ depending on how you set the scale, so depending on the method you use the power results you obtain might be different. The way to avoid this is to use a nested model, likelihood ratio test to test the significance of a parameter.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Power analysis Mimic model.... error messages
parts:
On 7/2/2015 2:24 PM, Christopher Lennartz wrote:
> model <- 'f =~ NA*x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5
> f ~ y
> f ~ z'

The metric of the latent variable 'f' seems undefined. You forced the
first factor loading to be free, but you did not fix the (residual)
variance of 'f'. Try adding

f ~~ 1*f # or any other constant you need

to your syntax, OR use std.lv = TRUE

Yves.
